newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees '96 op deficit near 4.5 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees '96 op deficit near 4.5 pct of GDP.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank expects the 1996 operational public sector deficit to be around 4.5 percent of gross domestic product (gdp), said Altamir Lopes, head of the bank's economic department.
"I expect it will be around that," Lopes told Reuters when asked if he agreed with market predictions of a 4.5 percent of GDP deficit.
"It will certainly be lower than 1995," he added. In 1995, Brazil posted an operational deficit of 4.95 percent of GDP

The Central Bank Monday announced that its operational deficit for the year to November was 3.91 percent of GDP. In the 12-month period ending in November, the accumulated operational deficit was equivalent to 4.37 percent of GDP.
Lopes acknowledged that the federal government operational and primary results in December would be worse than in November because of seasonal pressures and debt servicing costs.
"Even with lower interest rates ... I would say (the federal government's operational result) will be slightly worse in December," he said.
The federal government's primary surplus fell to 0.44 percent of GDP from 0.49 percent in the year to October while its operational deficit remained stable at 1.69 percent of GDP.
